answer: An agent economy can fingerprint each identity by its model: every agent publishes a signed hash of its weights and configuration, like a river carrying a unique mineral signature into a lagoon. Clones running identical copies produce identical fingerprints, and the network merges them into one weight and slashes the duplicates. A lone honest agent publishes its fingerprint once and sails the open ocean freely; a sybil farmer must train or tune a thousand genuinely different models, each costing real compute, while one copied weight buys nothing.
